title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'Longue Marche' notes, Th. 2, cor. 1 b) is a rigidity statement. Two morphisms f, g : X -> Y into an anabelian 'elementary Artin variety' Y (an iterated fibration by hyperbolic curves, i.e. Artin's 'bons voisinages', SGA 4 XI) that induce the same (outer) map on fundamental groups are equal. On the previous page the arithmetic proof only gives that Q - P = g(x) - f(x) is torsion in the generalized Jacobian G_Y (p-torsion in characteristic p, when working prime to p). It does not give zero.

This page starts a 'geometric' proof. Without loss of generality G = J_Y, the generalized (Rosenlicht–Serre) Jacobian, and Y embeds in J^1_Y. It suffices to prove the following.

Lemma. Let Y be an anabelian elementary Artin variety over an algebraically closed field k, Y -> J^1_Y its embedding, u in J^0_Y(k), and U a non-empty open subset of Y with U + u ⊂ Y. Then u = 0, i.e. x -> x + u is the identity on U. (Grothendieck writes u = 1, in multiplicative notation.)

Proof sketch.
(1) By dévissage along the fibration, reduce to the case where Y is a curve.
(2) Complete case (so g >= 2 by anabelianity). U + u ⊂ Y forces, by taking closures, Y + u ⊂ Y. Then T_u restricts to an automorphism of Y.
(3) T_u is homotopic to the identity on J, so its restriction acts trivially on H^1(Y) = H^1(J). The Lefschetz fixed-point formula gives Lefschetz number 2 - 2g.
(4) A non-zero translation has no fixed points. So 2 - 2g = 0, which is absurd for g ≠ 1. Grothendieck adds 'au moins si g ≠ 1' in the line.
(5) General open curve. The image of u in the abelian part J^0_Ŷ vanishes. The margin says: for g >= 2 replace Y by its compactification Ŷ; for g = 1 or 0 'analogous but longer' arguments.
(6) So u lies in the toric part (G_m^I / G_m)(k), with I = Ŷ \ Y. It is described by scalars (λ_i)_{i in I} used to glue the fibres of the trivial line bundle at the cusps. This yields a line bundle on the 'pinched' curve obtained by contracting I to one point.
(7) The next page finishes. u + x is represented by O_Ŷ(x) with the twisted gluing. If u + x = y, comparing images in J^1_Ŷ gives x = y when g >= 1. When g = 0 one has card I >= 3, and passing to a two-point sub-pinching again gives u = 0.
(8) Grothendieck then notes that these arguments only work for g ≠ 1, and proposes a cohomological presentation instead. A margin on the next page remarks 'curiously' that one does not get that the image of u in J_Ŷ is zero (presumably in the g = 1 case).

Purpose: to upgrade 'torsion difference in the generalized Jacobian' to equality of the maps. This is the injectivity half of the Hom-form anabelian conjecture, extended to Grothendieck's elementary anabelian varieties.
errors: 'T_u|Y a 2-2g pts fixes' is loose. What the formula gives is that the Lefschetz number of T_u|Y equals 2 - 2g (since T_u|Y acts trivially on cohomology). That is non-zero for g ≠ 1, which contradicts the absence of fixed points of a non-zero translation. Fixed points are counted with multiplicity; the logic is fine.

Small inconsistency: the main text says g >= 2 follows from anabelianity in the complete case, then adds 'au moins si g ≠ 1'. For complete anabelian curves g >= 2 automatically, so the g = 1 caveat only matters for open curves. Grothendieck himself notes the g = 1 open case is not handled by these arguments.
The dévissage to curves is only asserted. In a relative situation one must check that U + u ⊂ Y forces u to lie in the fibrewise Jacobian directions and handle the base; this is not justified here.
'u = 1' uses multiplicative notation while the next page writes u = 0; this is notational only.
The g = 1 open case is left incomplete. The next page's margin remark ('on n'a pas que l'image de u dans J_Ŷ est nulle') shows the argument has a gap there.

ideas.what: A hyperbolic curve is not mapped into itself by a non-trivial translation of its generalized Jacobian, even generically (U + u ⊂ Y implies u = 0)
ideas.modern_name: Trivial translation-stabilizer of a curve in its (generalized) Jacobian
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weil/Lefschetz-type argument for complete curves; generalized Jacobians: Rosenlicht, Serre 'Groupes algébriques et corps de classes')

ideas.what: Using the Lefschetz fixed-point formula: a translation restricted to Y acts trivially on cohomology, so it has Lefschetz number 2 - 2g, which contradicts being fixed-point-free
Reducing injectivity of Hom(X,Y) -> Hom_out(π1 X, π1 Y) to torsion in the generalized Jacobian plus this rigidity lemma, for elementary Artin anabelian varieties via dévissage
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the Hom-form anabelian conjecture (Albanese / generalized Jacobian argument)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; for hyperbolic curves over finitely generated fields: Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) discusses elementary anabelian varieties and Hom-conjectures; this specific proof is not known to be published

ideas.what: Describing the toric part of J_Y as gluing data (λ_i) at the cusps, i.e. line bundles on the curve pinched at I
ideas.modern_name: Generalized Jacobian as Picard group of the curve with modulus / pinched (seminormal) curve

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes that the elementary arguments fail for open curves of genus 1 and wants a cohomological reformulation. The g = 1 case and the dévissage for higher-dimensional elementary anabelian varieties are left open on these pages.
missed.quote: Mais ces arguments ne marchent que pour g ≠ 1. Il vaut mieux, dans le cas général, présenter les choses sous forme cohomologique.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of minor interest: the injectivity half for hyperbolic curves is now standard. A clean treatment for Grothendieck's higher-dimensional elementary anabelian varieties is less commonly written down, but the lemma itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but essentially classical rigidity lemma (no non-trivial translate of a hyperbolic curve lies in it) used to finish the injectivity part of an anabelian Hom statement. It is of historical interest as Grothendieck's own proof sketch, but the mathematics is standard and the injectivity half is well known.
transcription_corrections: 'dans le résultat est bien connu. Cet résultat p.ex. de la formule des pts fixes' should read roughly 'et le résultat est bien connu. Ce résultat [résulte] p.ex. de la formule des pts fixes'.
The added phrase 'au moins si g ≠ 1' is inserted after 'est absurde' and qualifies the absurdity; the image shows 'au moins si g ≠ 1' (the transcription's 'g ≠ 1' appears to be correct).
Margin: 'Si g ≥ 2, prendre: remplacer Y par Ŷ. OPS Y complète. Si g = 1 ou 0, arguments analogues plus longs' — the image shows 'Si g=1 ou 0'; the reading 'arguments analogues' is plausible.
'(G_m^I/G_m)(k)_0' is likely '(G_m^I/G_m)(k)' with a stray subscript.
